title: Support Operations Analysis Report
executive_summary: Analysis of 220 support tickets reveals a total labor cost of $17,445.07 and a mean resolution time of 75.7 minutes. Team Beta carries the highest labor cost share. Chat resolves fastest on average, while email tickets reopen at a rate more than twice that of chat. A small high-cost, low-satisfaction segment warrants targeted intervention. Agent workload is moderately concentrated, with the busiest agent handling 7.3% of all tickets.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 220 tickets with a mean resolution time of 75.7 minutes and a total labor cost of $17,445.07.
Team Beta incurred the highest labor cost at $6,928.72, followed by Gamma at $5,911.44 and Alpha at $4,604.91. Beta's cost exceeds Alpha's by $2,323.81.
Email tickets resolved fastest on average at 71.7 minutes, followed by phone at 74.1 minutes, while chat was slowest at 82.2 minutes.
Email tickets reopen at 15.2%, compared to 6.8% for chat — an increase of 122.5% relative to the chat reopen rate, indicating email tickets are substantially more likely to require reopening.
Nine tickets met the high-cost (labor_cost ≥ $100) and low-satisfaction (score ≤ 2) criteria, with 11.1% of them having been reopened — a segment meriting priority review.

Resolution time has a median of 65.0 minutes and a sample standard deviation of 51.3 minutes, indicating notable spread. The mean satisfaction score among the 206 tickets with valid responses is 4.14 out of 5; 14 tickets have missing satisfaction scores.
Tickets were handled by 18 distinct agents. The busiest single agent handled 16 tickets, representing 7.3% of total volume — a moderate but not extreme concentration.

limitations: Both the cleaning and analysis pipeline stages reported validation failures; results should be treated as provisional until the underlying data quality issues are investigated and resolved.
Fourteen tickets (6.4% of the dataset) have missing satisfaction scores, which may introduce bias into satisfaction-related metrics if missingness is non-random.
The high-cost, low-satisfaction segment contains only 9 tickets, making percentage-based metrics for that group statistically fragile.
Agent identity is represented only by agent_id; without roster metadata it is impossible to assess whether workload concentration reflects specialisation, staffing gaps, or data errors.
Resolution time spread (std ≈ 51 minutes vs. median 65 minutes) suggests possible outliers that could distort mean-based comparisons across channels and teams.
conclusion: Support operations show acceptable overall satisfaction (mean 4.14) but elevated email reopen rates (+122% vs. chat) and a costly low-satisfaction segment that together represent the clearest opportunities for improvement. Team Beta's disproportionate labor cost and the wide dispersion in resolution times also warrant further investigation. All findings should be re-validated once the data pipeline failures are resolved.
